name: Arthur Henry Hallam
credit: Drawing of the bust of Arthur Henry Hallam by Francis Chantrey, published 1898 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Arthur Henry Hallam (1811–1833) was an English poet and essayist, the close friend of Alfred Tennyson whose early death inspired In Memoriam.

The poems here are taken from Alfred H. Miles (ed.), The Poets and the Poetry of the Century (London: Hutchinson, 1891–1897), vol. 4, from the Internet Archive scans of that edition. Spelling is that of the anthology; Miles's biographical essay and extracts from longer poems are omitted, and only poems that could be read cleanly from the scan are included.

poems.title: Sonnet. (To My Mother)
poems.author: Arthur Henry Hallam
poems.text:
When barren doubt like a late-coming snow,
Made an unkind December of my spring,
That all the pretty flowers did droop for woe,
And the sweet birds their love no more would sing;
Then the remembrance of thy gentle faith,
Mother beloved, would steal upon my heart;
Fond feeling saved me from that utter scathe,
And from thy hope I could not live apart.
Now that my mind hath passed from wintry gloom,
And on the calmed waters once again
Ascendant Faith circles with silver plume,
That casts a charmed shade, not now in pain,
Thou child of Christ, in joy I think of thee,
And mingle prayers for what we both may be.
